title: Chicken Tacos
subtitle: Shredded spiced chicken in warm corn tortillas
excerpt: Juicy shredded chicken cooked with cumin, smoked paprika, and garlic, served in warm corn tortillas with avocado, soured cream, and fresh coriander. Ready in 30 minutes from start to table.
sourceNotes: Tex-Mex shredded chicken tacos: a US home-cooking staple derived from Mexican taco tradition adapted for the Anglo-American pantry. Based on classic Tex-Mex home-cooking canon.

recipe.freezeNotes: The cooked shredded chicken freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the chicken quantity and freeze half for a quick future meal.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and shred the chicken up to 2 days ahead; reheat in a pan with a splash of water.

content.text: Chicken tacos are soft corn tortillas filled with shredded spiced chicken, finished with cool toppings at the table. Boneless chicken thighs stay juicy and shred easily once cooked through; the spice mix takes a minute to pull together from pantry staples. Corn tortillas warm directly in a dry pan in about 30 seconds a side.
A tortilla pan (comal) or a dry cast-iron skillet is ideal for warming the tortillas, but any frying pan works fine.
Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, garlic, lime juice, and olive oil in a bowl. Toss the chicken thighs through the marinade to coat.
Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken thighs for 6-7 minutes on each side until cooked through and slightly charred at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes, then shred with two forks.
Heat a dry frying pan or tortilla pan over high heat. Warm each tortilla for 30-45 seconds on each side until lightly charred in spots. Stack and wrap in a clean tea towel to keep warm.
Set out the shredded chicken, sliced avocado, soured cream, coriander, red onion, and lime wedges. Each person builds their own tacos.

items.symptom: The chicken is dry and stringy
items.cause: Overcooked, or cooked too fast without resting
items.fix: Thighs need a 5-minute rest before shredding. The juices redistribute and the meat stays moist.

items.cause: Corn tortillas were not warmed enough; cold corn tortillas crack
items.fix: Warm each one in a dry pan until it bends without snapping. A damp cloth over the stack while warming also helps.

items.symptom: Bland flavour despite the spice mix
items.cause: Not enough salt, or the marinade wasn't rubbed in properly
items.fix: Season the chicken well with salt before and after cooking. The spices need salt to taste like anything.
Slice it just before serving. A squeeze of lime over the slices slows browning.

content.text: Use chicken breast instead of thighs for a leaner result, though thighs stay moister under high heat. For a richer finish, cook the chicken in a pan with a little stock and shred it in the liquid rather than dry-roasting it.

Chicken tacos sit in the everyday Tex-Mex register: quick enough for a weeknight, flexible enough to feed a crowd, and adaptable to whatever toppings are on hand. The corn tortilla is the constant; everything else moves with the season and the fridge.
